cards.text: When David, Israel's king, is old and full of years, he installs his son Solomon as king over Israel. Then he gathers all the leaders of Israel, plus the priests and the Levites. Big meeting, friend. The kind where NOBODY is checking their phone.
First, a head count of every Levite man thirty and older: 38,000. That is a LOT of name tags.

cards.question: David splits the 38,000 Levites into four groups. The biggest group, 24,000 men, gets which job?

answers.text: Oversee the work of the LORD's house
Keep watch at the city gates

cards.question: Next, David says 6,000 Levites are to be officers and ___.
The last 8,000 Levites get split right down the middle. 4,000 become gatekeepers. What are the other 4,000 to do?

cards.text: And those instruments? David says he made them himself. Friend, I built ONE cookie box from scratch, and it folded before the first batch even cooled.

Then David divides the Levites into divisions by Levi's three sons, Gershon, Kohath and Merari, and the list runs family by family, every head of a family registered by name. One standout: Aaron, Moses' brother, and his descendants are set apart forever to consecrate the most holy things, burn incense before the LORD, minister before Him and pronounce blessings in His name.
Then comes what David had said, plain as day: "The LORD, the God of Israel, has given rest to His people and has come to dwell in Jerusalem forever."

cards.question: Since the LORD has come to dwell in Jerusalem, David says the Levites no longer need to ___ the tabernacle.

cards.text: No more hauling the tabernacle and all its articles around. I moved ONE time, from a kitchen counter to a junk drawer, and I am STILL not over it.

cards.question: Earlier, David counted the Levites thirty and older. True or false: by David's final instructions, the Levites twenty and older are counted.

cards.text: So if nobody's carrying a tent anymore, what's the job? The Levites become helpers in the service of the house of the LORD.

cards.question: The Levites are to assist with the service of the LORD's house. Who are they assisting?
The Levites are told to stay out of the courts and chambers of the LORD's house.

cards.text: Then the job list gets to the bread: the rows of the showbread, the fine flour for the grain offering and the wafers of unleavened bread. Friend. FRIEND. There are BAKERS in the house of the LORD, and I have never felt so seen in my life.

cards.question: The Levites also handle the baking, the mixing and all ___ of quantity and size.
On top of all that work, the Levites have a set time to stand and give thanks and praise to the LORD. When is it?

cards.text: And whenever burnt offerings are presented to the LORD on the Sabbaths, New Moons and appointed feasts, the Levites serve regularly, in the numbers set for them. Morning shift, evening shift AND holidays, friend. That schedule does NOT come with a snooze button.

cards.question: To wrap it all up, the Levites are put in charge over the descendants of Aaron.

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: "When David... over Israel." "Then he gathers... the Levites." "Big meeting, friend." "The kind where NOBODY is checking their phone."

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the next word of David's line, "officers and ___" (v4). Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason their way to "judges" over "singers" or "scribes". It tests wording they haven't seen, not meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card says "David says he made them himself." The BSB has "the instruments I have made" (v5), which doesn't say whether David crafted them personally. "Himself" stretches the text. This card also has 3 sentences.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences: "And those instruments?" "David says he made them himself." "Friend, I built ONE cookie box..."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Moses appears for the first time here and is used only to identify Aaron ("Aaron, Moses' brother"). Moses himself is never introduced.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The story card has 4 sentences: "Then the job list... unleavened bread." "Friend." "FRIEND." "There are BAKERS..."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences: "And whenever burnt offerings... set for them." "Morning shift, evening shift AND holidays, friend." "That schedule does NOT come with a snooze button."
